statement_en: What is the sign of the membrane-potential change by which kcnk5b gain of function (the zebrafish alf alleles) drives fin overgrowth, in the tissue where the growth happens?
found_by: Found by trying to FORMALISE the dispute. The repo recorded it as "the papers disagree on sign" (genotype/CAUSAL.md row kcnk5b). Writing both arms as named Lean hypotheses forced a check of which paper asserts which sign, and the attribution did not survive: the sentence proposing that both signs occur sequentially is Jiang 2024's OWN, so Jiang reconciles Perathoner rather than contradicting him. The question has three arms, not two, and the two published readings are provably not formally contradictory. Attempting a precise statement is what exposed that the arms were misdescribed.

arms.statement_en: Raising the kcnk5b K+ leak conductance makes the membrane potential MORE NEGATIVE (hyperpolarisation), and that is the signal that drives overgrowth.

arms.position: biphasic (a named alternative, not a side)
arms.statement_en: Both signs occur in ONE cell at different times: the raised K+ leak first hyperpolarises, and that change then activates Na+ channels which depolarise the cell. The sign of "the" membrane-potential change is therefore not a property of the genotype alone, and both published readings are correct for the phase and preparation each sampled.

evidence.claim: No evidence held by this repository contradicts the biphasic arm: a biphasic cell reproduces both published readings, which is proved in Lean.
evidence.quote: A biphasic cell supplies an arm-`hyperpolarising` reading when sampled early and an arm-`depolarising` reading when sampled late, from the one cell. So the published observations do not between them exclude the third arm, and a law asserting either of the first two would assert more than the evidence settles.
evidence.kind: Lean proof that the arm is not excluded by either published reading

exclusivity.statement: Arms `hyperpolarising` and `depolarising` are PROVED mutually exclusive only once the premise `SamePreparation` is added (the two readings are of the same cell at the same steady state): Delphi.OpenQuestion.KcnkSign.arms_exclusive_same_preparation. WITHOUT that premise they are both inhabited at once (arms_not_exclusive_without_same_preparation), so the two papers are NOT formally contradictory -- they are empirically unresolved in the tissue that matters. Arm `biphasic` is excluded by neither (biphasic_supplies_both_readings). Forcing this into a two-sided contradiction would misrepresent what Jiang 2024 actually claims.
exclusivity.premise: SamePreparation: that the hyperpolarisation reading and the depolarisation reading are of the same cell type at the same steady state. Nothing in any fetched source inhabits it -- Perathoner et al. recorded Xenopus oocytes and Jiang et al. recorded zebrafish fin-bud cells.

what_would_settle_it.observation: The steady-state resting membrane potential of wild-type and alf mutant pectoral-fin-bud cells, same stage, same recording method, measured in the fish.
what_would_settle_it.how: Whole-cell patch clamp or a calibrated voltage-sensitive dye on fin-bud mesenchyme at 32-72 hpf in wild-type and alf siblings, reporting absolute mV for both genotypes rather than a relative change.
what_would_settle_it.why_decisive: It inhabits SamePreparation, which is the premise arms_exclusive_same_preparation needs; the sign of vmMut - vmWt then eliminates one of the first two arms outright, and its agreement or disagreement with a time course decides between the survivor and biphasic.
what_would_settle_it.feasibility_note: Both techniques are standard in zebrafish fin buds; Jiang et al. 2024 already used DiSBAC2(3) membrane-potential imaging in this tissue, so the gap is a reported absolute value, not a missing method.

what_would_settle_it.observation: A time course of membrane potential in one alf fin-bud cell from the onset of channel activity.
what_would_settle_it.how: Simultaneous voltage imaging and Na+-channel block (the inhibitors Jiang et al. 2024 already used), sampling fast enough to resolve an early transient.
what_would_settle_it.why_decisive: A transient hyperpolarisation followed by depolarisation inhabits BiphasicResponse directly and confirms arm biphasic; its absence refutes that arm and leaves the two sign arms.

what_would_settle_it.observation: Whether the oocyte and the fin-bud cell differ in Na+-channel complement sufficiently to flip the net sign.
what_would_settle_it.how: Compare the voltage-gated Na+ channel transcripts present in Xenopus oocytes with those in zebrafish fin-bud mesenchyme, then test whether adding the fin-bud complement to the oocyte flips the sign.
what_would_settle_it.why_decisive: It tests the mechanism the biphasic arm asserts, and it would explain the preparation difference rather than merely recording it.

known_gaps: nanopubs-index/README.md records that "The contradiction should be restated over six sources, not three, and the 'which sign?' framing may be the wrong question", naming PMID 33830014 (doi:10.7554/eLife.60691) and PMID 31472116 (doi:10.1016/j.ydbio.2019.08.016) as two further sources this record does not yet read. Those two papers have NOT been fetched by this thread, so no arm rests on them and no evidence item cites them.
md/kcnk5b/README.md states what all-atom MD can and cannot do here: "MD cannot settle the cell-level sign: that depends on the cell's other conductances." The MD results therefore appear in no arm.
